headline: Medicine works with your body—helping it do what it already knows how to do
universal_truth: Healing usually means supporting natural processes, not replacing them
fun_facts: Aspirin was derived from willow bark—a folk remedy used for thousands of years before we understood why it worked
Antibiotics don't kill viruses—they only work on bacteria
Your body heals most minor injuries and illnesses on its own; medicine often just helps it along
discussion_questions: What's the difference between treating symptoms and curing disease?
Why do some treatments work for some people but not others?
How has medicine changed human lifespan?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Medicine seems like magic—swallow a pill, feel better. But most medicine isn't replacing your body's healing; it's supporting it. Your body knows how to heal. Medicine removes obstacles, fights invaders, or manages processes your body handles naturally.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We have pills, injections, surgeries, and therapies. But how does medicine actually heal? What's happening when you take a drug and get better?

options.text: They assist or modulate natural body processes—fighting pathogens, reducing inflammation, or supporting healing
options.response: Yes. Medicine usually works with your body: killing germs it can't handle, reducing overactive responses, or providing what's missing.

options.text: They contain healing substances that directly repair damage
options.response: Some do provide missing substances, but most work by modulating your body's own systems...

q1.title: Fighting Invaders
q1.script: Antibiotics don't heal you—they kill bacteria. Your immune system handles the rest. Antivirals work differently, often stopping viruses from replicating. Medicine provides reinforcements for battles your body is already fighting.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Fighting Invaders"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Managing Processes
q2.script: Many medicines modulate—they turn processes up or down. Pain relievers reduce inflammation. Blood pressure medicine relaxes vessels. Insulin replaces what diabetics can't make. They adjust dials, not rebuild systems.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: From Folk to Science
q3.script: Many modern medicines have ancient roots. Aspirin came from willow bark. Digitalis from foxglove. Morphine from poppies. Science identified what worked and why—but the healing started with observation and tradition.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Healing usually means supporting natural processes. Medicine teaches that your body has remarkable healing ability. Most treatment is helping your body do what it already knows—just faster or more effectively.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 126. Tomorrow, we'll explore training your immune system—vaccines. Until then, appreciate that your body is already a healing machine; medicine just helps it along.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Healing Partnership - Support Your Body
growTrack.learning_objective: See medicine as supporting natural healing
growTrack.activity: Next time you take medicine, consider what it's actually doing: fighting invaders, reducing inflammation, or replacing something missing. Medicine is a partnership with your body's healing systems. What else can you do to support those systems?
